text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Unregistered political associations have been warned against holding meetings or attempting to join with any registered political party.
- Applicants wishing to acquire mobile telephones will be required to give details of their business and then vetted by the state-run operator to ensure that fraudsters are unable to subscribe.
- Both Nigeria and Cameroon made proposals to restore confidence between them during a United Nations mission last month to the disputed Bakassi peninsula in the oil-rich Gulf of Guinea.
- Nigeria and Indonesia are currently working on a memorandum of understanding on mutual aid and cooperation in development of solid minerals.
- Privatisation of state-run Nigerian Telecommunications could result in the loss of 7,000 jobs.
- Some interest rates at some banks rose by one percentage point as the central bank's announcement that it had lifted the interest rate ceiling took hold.
- National Electric Power Authority may cut off the government of southwestern Ogun state if it fails to pay its bills.
- Air Afrique will start flights from Lagos to New York on October 27. The airline will get around an Amercian ban on direct flights by stopping at it's Abidjan base for 30 minutes on the way out.
